key_insight: A compact trefoil vortex knot with a Rosenhead profile can evolve in decaying Navier–Stokes simulations to produce turbulence-like Kolmogorov spectra and structure-function scaling.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a controlled numerical route to generate fully developed turbulent statistics from an unforced, boundary-free initial condition for comparison with experiments.
method: Extend the trefoil vortex simulation to later times in a larger (4π)^3 periodic domain
Use an algebraic Rosenhead vorticity profile to improve compactness and enable finite energy dissipation
Analyze energy spectra, energy decay, integral-scale growth, and higher-order vorticity moments
evidence_signal: The abstract reports persistent Kolmogorov scaling, structure-function scaling, ν-independent finite energy dissipation, and exponents E(t)~(t+t0)^-10/7 and ℓ(t)~(t+t0)^2/7 consistent with Loitsyanskii-invariant arguments.
watch_item: The agreement with the experimental integral-scale growth rate depends on excluding Fourier modes near the periodic-domain scale, so domain-size effects may influence the conclusions.
paper_title: Generating Kolmogorov spectra and structure functions with a Rosenhead profile trefoil vortex knot
